title: 5 Questions to Ask Before Signing a Commercial Lease
excerpt: A practical checklist for checking occupancy costs, lease obligations, permitted use, flexibility and professional advice before you commit.
author: Joe Kelley
metaTitle: 5 Questions Before Signing a Commercial Lease | YOS
metaDescription: Check occupancy costs, make-good, rent reviews, permitted use and flexibility before signing a commercial lease.
body:
A commercial lease can shape your operating costs and flexibility for years. Before committing, slow the process down and get clear answers to five questions.

## 1. What will occupancy really cost?

Look beyond the advertised rent. Ask for a written schedule covering outgoings, taxes where applicable, parking, utilities, maintenance, management charges and any other recurring costs. Compare proposals on the same assumptions and over the same period.

## 2. What will you need to do when the lease ends?

Make-good obligations can require removal of fitout, repairs or reinstatement. Ask your legal adviser to explain the clause, record the starting condition of the premises and identify what can be negotiated before signing.

## 3. How can the rent change?

Check the timing and method of every review. Model the full lease term, including option periods you may exercise. If a market review applies, understand the process, evidence requirements and dispute mechanism.

## 4. Does the permitted use match the business?

List what your team does today and what may change. Check that the lease, planning controls, building rules and any required approvals can accommodate those activities. Written confirmation matters.

## 5. What flexibility do you have?

Review assignment, subletting, expansion, contraction, renewal and any break rights. A clause is only useful if its conditions are practical for your business.

## Before you sign

Tenant representation supports the commercial comparison and negotiation process. It does not replace independent legal, financial, planning or tax advice. Bring those advisers in before you become bound.
